newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies, hogs gain on strong cash prices.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies, hogs gain on strong cash prices.

text.p: CME pork belly futures rose the 3.00 cent per lb daily limit at mid-morning and hog futures posted strong gains in reaction to tight supplies of market-ready hogs and higher prices for some pork items analysts and traders said.

Cash hogs traded mostly $1.00 per cwt higher at key Midwest markets Thursday. Analysts said a decline in the number of market-ready hogs has forced packers to bid higher to ensure slaughter needs were covered.
USDA late Wednesday reported cash prices for 12- to-14-lb fresh bellies rose $2.50 per cwt to $87.00, versus $82.50 on Friday.

Also hog slaughter this week has trailed week-ago and year-ago levels. On Wednesday, USDA reported week-to-date hog slaughter at 946,000 head, below 1.038 million the previous week and 1.055 million a year ago.
Some traders said rumors that swine fever was found in the Spainsh hog herd contributed to gains, but analysts doubted that was the reason for the gains.

At 1042 CDT, pork bellies were up 2.575 to 3.00 cents with May up 2.575 at 94.700 cents per lb. Earlier, the May contract jumped up the 3.00-cent limit to a contract high of 95.125. Contract highs were set in all pork belly contracts in morning trading.
Hogs were up 0.700 to 0.250 cent with June up the most at 85.650 cents, after earlier setting a contract high of 85.950 cents. Contract highs were also set in the eight nearby hog contracts.
